title: TfModule Demo

# TfModule

A `<TfModule>` block draws its form from an OpenTofu module. The module's `variables.tf` gives each input's name, type, default and validation; its `runbook_block.yml` says how to present them.

This runbook uses a copy of the `google-group` module from the catalog. Open it with `--simulate` so the organization dropdown, the people suggestions, and the plan and apply on the **Apply** tab answer from [simulation.yml](./simulation.yml) instead of your Google Workspace:

```bash
runbooks open --simulate testdata/feature-demos/tf-module
```

## Describe the group

<TfModule
  id="group"
  source="google-group"
  template="templates/google-group-unit"
  path="google-groups/{{ .id }}"
/>

The runbook decides how to use the module: [its template](./templates/google-group-unit) renders a Terragrunt unit. The **Code** tab shows that unit with these values, in its folder in the repository, which simulation.yml stands in for here; the **PR** tab opens a GitHub pull request that adds the code under `google-groups/` in the repository a `<GitClone>` block cloned, and the **Apply** tab plans and applies it. Merge and apply in either order. Once it applies, the module's outputs are the block's outputs, such as `{{ .outputs.group.runbooks_console_url }}`.

## Use the values

Other blocks read the module's inputs through `inputsId`, as they read an `<Inputs>` block's.

<Command
  id="show-group"
  title="Show the group's inputs"
  inputsId="group"
  env={{
    GROUP_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.id }}",
    GROUP_NAME: "{{ .inputs.display_name }}",
    GROUP_DOMAIN: "{{ .inputs.domain }}",
  }}
  command={`echo "Group:  $GROUP_EMAIL"
echo "Name:   $GROUP_NAME"
echo "Domain: $GROUP_DOMAIN"
echo "group_email=$GROUP_EMAIL" >> "$RUNBOOK_OUTPUT"`}
/>
